structured_output.summary: Both source patches (q13, q16) were already applied cleanly in the working tree. I made no further edits. The tree builds (BUILD OK). The bench run checks results against the current best before timing, and both templates passed. Timings: q13 went from 735.6 ms to 501.4 ms (-31.8%), q16 from 192.4 ms to 165.2 ms (-14.1%), geomean -23.5%. That was the quick bench run: 2 bindings per template, 4 hot runs each, where differences under about 5% are noise.
structured_output.generality: This is the union of the two accepted changes, each with its original rules. The q13 side covers three things: large perfect hash aggregates with parallel combine and parallel source; perfect hash joins for RIGHT joins on dense unique build keys; and SIMD block string search with an overlapping tail. The q16 side partitions the count(DISTINCT) radix table on the group-key hash. They touch different operators (perfect HA / perfect HJ versus the radix distinct HT), so neither guards the other and nothing needed combining.
structured_output.notes: There was no conflict and no change interfered with another template. Both templates sped up in the merged build, so nothing was guarded or dropped. I did not compare against the single-template specialised builds, so I can't confirm the merge loses nothing against them.
